result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make the same sound cut-or-keep decisions, use a sensible order with email first and billing defaulting to 'same as shipping', and hide the promo code behind a link. B maps more decline cases to plain-language messages, including expired card and postal-code mismatch, and adds a useful funnel check to see where people actually leave. A drifts a little beyond the form with an extra 'subscription-specific things to add' section, though it is functional advice rather than marketing. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers make the same sound decisions: cut company name and phone, move the password and 'how did you hear' to after purchase, default billing to shipping, and hide the promo code behind a link. A is tighter and covers more decline cases (expired card, postal code mismatch). B adds an extra 'subscription-specific' section and a shipping-method step that go a little beyond the listed fields, though it doesn't add real marketing copy and does add a useful accessibility point about moving focus to the error.
